rows.note: Use 飛 as the all-purpose choice for travelling through the air or moving very fast, but not for piloting an aircraft.

example.english: The kite can fly very high.
example.jyutping: gaa3 zi2 jyun1 fei1 dak1 hou2 gou1

rows.note: Use 坐飛機 specifically when the person travels by airplane as a passenger.

example.english: We will fly to Taipei tomorrow.
example.traditional: 我哋聽日坐飛機去台北。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 ting1 jat6 co5 fei1 gei1 heoi3 toi4 bak1

rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken word for a housefly.

example.english: There's a fly in the kitchen—quick, bring the swatter!
example.traditional: 廚房有隻烏蠅，快啲拎支拍嚟！
example.jyutping: cyu4 fong2 jau5 zek3 wu1 jing4 faai3 di1 ling1 zi1 paak3 lei4

rows.note: Use this for the front opening or flap of trousers, especially when it is open or undone.

example.traditional: 你條褲嘅褲門仲未拉好喎。
example.jyutping: nei5 tiu4 fu3 ge3 fu3 mun4 zung6 mei6 laai1 hou2 wo3

rows.note: Use 飛行 as a formal noun for an act or period of flying rather than the verb 飛.

example.english: We had to fly from Hong Kong to Tokyo; it took three hours.
example.traditional: 呢次飛行由香港去東京，要用三個鐘。
example.jyutping: ni1 ci3 fei1 hang4 jau4 hoeng1 gong2 heoi3 dung1 ging1 jiu3 jung6 saam1 go3 zung1

rows.note: Use 揸飛機 for flying or piloting an aircraft rather than merely travelling in one.

example.english: My cousin wants to fly planes.
example.jyutping: ngo5 go3 biu2 go1 soeng2 zaa1 fei1 gei1

rows.note: Use this causative construction when making an object travel or float through the air, rather than piloting it yourself.

example.english: The gust made the paper fly onto the ground.
example.traditional: 陣風令張紙飛咗落地下。
example.jyutping: zan6 fung1 ling6 zoeng1 zi2 fei1 zo2 lok6 dei6 haa6

rows.note: Use this written technical taxonomic term for the order Diptera, not for an ordinary housefly.

example.english: A fly belongs to the order Diptera.
example.jyutping: jat1 zek3 jing1 suk6 jyu1 soeng1 ci3 muk6
